full_text_zh:
[P1] 天上的帆船
文/图: [英] 昆廷·布莱克 翻译: 梅思繁
北京联合出版公司

[P3] 天上的帆船
文/图：（英）昆廷·布莱克
翻译：杨忠繁
北京联合出版公司

[P4] 伊莎贝尔和尼古拉在沙滩上散步。
他们随意地穿过一个又一个沙丘。

[P5] “看，尼古拉！有一艘破得不成形的帆船！
“我看这船还能用，来，我们一起把它拔出来！”

“轮子应该是和这块木头接在一起……”
“尼古拉，我觉得这艘船看起来有点儿古怪。”

[P6] 沙丘上吹起了一阵阵海风。
船帆被风吹得鼓鼓的，
船居然慢慢地在沙滩上滑行起来。
“你看那儿！”伊莎贝尔喊。

“我叫西多尼，是一只受伤的鹳。
我的肩膀被子弹打伤了，不能像从前
那样在天上飞翔了。”

[P7] 海风越来越猛烈，帆船滑得越来越快。
这时，天上飞来了一群鹅。

帆船慢慢离开了地面，在空中飞了起来。
“快上来！”
尼古拉和伊莎贝尔伸出双手。

于是，西多尼跟着他们一起飞上了天空。

一只有着巨大翅膀的
鹅向帆船飞来，它的名字
叫古斯。
古斯扯着嗓子喊：“你们既然救了西多尼，那就再多做些
好事吧。从我这里望过去，还有很多和西多尼一样无法在天空飞翔的鹅。”
“我们是不是也应该帮助它们？”尼古拉问。
“当然！”伊莎贝尔说，“让古斯为我们带路。”

[P8] 帆船飞着飞着，来到了另一片沙滩的上空。
一群野蛮的男孩正在追打一个女孩。
“他们用石头扔她！”西多尼喊了起来，“这样会打伤她的，
说不定正好就打伤她的肩膀。”

“快上来！”伊莎贝尔把手伸向女孩，“我们的船一定会保护你的。”
小女孩被拉上了船，她叫艾卢伊斯。

[P9] 从广阔的天空俯视下去，大地一望无际。
远远地，伊莎贝尔和尼古拉望见一群男人正在劳动。
在他们当中，有几个又瘦又小的男孩，也挥动着锄头。
其中的一个男孩，他实在太瘦弱了，看上去连举起锄头的力气都没有。
帆船几乎擦着地面飞驰而过。
伊莎贝尔、尼古拉和艾卢伊斯把筋疲力尽的男孩拉进船里。这个新朋友叫拉希德。
艾卢伊斯用拉希德的破烂围巾替他擦掉额头的汗水。
西多尼把自己的羽毛给拉希德当靠垫。

[P10] “那片黑乎乎的烟雾是什么？”伊莎贝尔叫道。

[P11] “看，我们在一座巨大的城市上方，这里所有的东西都在冒烟！房子、工厂、汽车、人……”

艾卢伊斯话还没说完，就咳嗽起来。
拉希德和尼古拉也捂着鼻子不停地咳嗽。
连西多尼也不例外。
伊莎贝尔生气地喊：“那些人难道没看见那个男孩吗？
他快被烟雾熏得喘不过气了！”

[P12] “这回轮到我行动了！”
古斯说着就钻进浓重的烟雾。

[P13] 拉希德对男孩说：‘大口呼吸，埃里克！这儿的空气
是不是特别清新？’
六个乘客随着帆船在空中自由地飘荡。
忽然，空中响起一阵阵沉闷的巨响。
‘我可从来都不害怕暴风雨！’伊莎贝尔大声地说。

[P14] 这巨大的响声不是闪电，也不是雷鸣，而是炮弹的轰击声和机枪的扫射声。
帆船里的孩子们吓得紧紧地蜷缩在一起。
西多尼探出脑袋往外看："有个女人抱着孩子在逃命……"

"得赶快离开这里！"伊莎贝尔叫了起来，"等等，我们应该去救他们！"

[P15] “一定是女人
怀里的孩子看见
了我们的帆船。”
西多尼说。

所有的人都伸出手来，西多尼用上了它的爪子，大家把这个叫玛格达的
女人和她的孩子里拉安置到船上。

帆船重新飞上了天空，小心地
躲进四处飞来的子弹。

[P16] 可是，船身被打穿了，船帆也破了好几个洞。帆船摇摇晃晃地失去了方向。

[P17] 终于又来到了海滩。
“我们可以在这里靠岸。”尼古拉说。
“小心，那里有个巫婆！”伊莎贝尔喊

[P18] “不是的，她是我外婆！”艾卢伊斯第一个下船，“外婆在这里卖鱼，大家都认识她！”，

[P19] 所有的人一起动手，把船身翻了过来，让玛格达和里拉休息。
伊莎贝尔和埃里克取下船帆，做成了吊床。
拉希德搬来了木柴给大家生火。
尼古拉拆下帆船的一个轮子当晾衣架。
西多尼和古斯则把另外一个轮子做成它们的鸟巢。
艾卢伊斯和外婆一起给大家做饭吃。

[P20] 外婆做的鱼汤鲜美无比。她还在鱼汤里加了一条“会飞的鱼”，好让西多尼的肩膀早点儿好起来。
“真希望你们能在我这儿多待些时间。”外婆说。
“可是，我们都有各自的家人……”尼古拉回答。
“还有朋友……”拉希德补充。
“而且，我们还有很多重要的旅行……”古斯说。
就在这时，拉希德指着海滩上一栋废弃的木屋：“用那些木板，我们也许可以做一艘比现在还大三倍又会飞的帆船！”

[P21] 外婆兴奋地站起来："拉希德说得对！我去把我的旧床单、旧裙子和旧手帕都找出来，我要给你们缝一张世界上最大最美丽的船帆！"
这个时候，西多尼慢慢地飞向空中："哇，我又能飞起来了！谁想骑到我的背上來？"

[P22] “明天黎明时分，我们就出发！”尼古拉说，“坐着我们的帆船，飞向广阔无际的天空……”

[P23] 本书的作者署名是英国的昆廷·布莱克，但并非由他一个人完成。来自新加坡、英国、爱尔兰、法国以及挪威的1800个孩子帮助他一起完成了这本绘本。
在这一年中，这些孩子用文字、图画、邮件与昆廷·布莱克交流，谈论着他们眼中共同的家园——地球面临的各种问题：战乱、污染、雇用童工和战争……在倾听孩子们对一个更温暖、更美好的世界的期待与梦想之后，昆廷·布莱克创作了《天上的帆船》。
感谢热内维耶芙·鲁加以及阅读启蒙协会（LSA-17），他们是这个项目的创始人及协调者，感谢所有参与该项目的孩子们，他们的名字被印在本书的环衬上。

full_text_en:
[P1] Sailing Ships in the Sky
Text & Illustrations: [UK] Quentin Blake Translation: Mei Sifan
Beijing United Publishing Company

[P3] Sailboats in the Sky
Text and Illustrations: (UK) Quentin Blake
Translated by: Yang Zhongfan
Beijing United Publishing Company

[P4] Isabelle and Nicolas are walking on the beach.
They casually pass through one sand dune after another.

[P5] "Look, Nicolas! There's a broken-down sailboat that's barely recognizable!"
"I think this boat can still be used. Come on, let's pull it out together!"

"The wheels should be attached to this piece of wood..."
"Nicolas, I think this boat looks a bit strange."

[P6] A sea breeze blew up over the dunes.
The sail puffed out, and the boat began to glide slowly across the sand.
"Look over there!" Isabelle shouted.

"My name is Sidonie. I'm an injured stork.
My shoulder was shot by a bullet. I can't fly in the sky like before."

[P7] The sea wind grew stronger and stronger, and the sailboat slid faster and faster.
At this moment, a flock of geese flew down from the sky.

The sailboat slowly lifted off the ground and began to fly through the air.
"Come on up!"
Nicolas and Isabelle stretched out their hands.

So, Sidonie flew up into the sky with them.

A goose with enormous wings flew toward the sailboat. Its name was Gus.
Gus shouted, "Since you saved Sidonie, you should do more good deeds. From here, I can see many more geese like Sidonie who can't fly in the sky."
"Shouldn't we help them too?" Nicolas asked.
"Of course!" Isabelle said. "Let Gus lead the way."

[P8] The sailboat flew and flew, arriving above another sandy beach.
A group of wild boys were chasing and hitting a girl.
“They’re throwing stones at her!” cried Sidonie, “That will hurt her,
maybe even hurt her shoulder.”

“Come on up!” Isabelle reached out to the girl, “Our boat will protect you.”
The little girl was pulled onto the boat. Her name was Elouise.

[P9] From the vast sky looking down, the earth stretched endlessly.
Far away, Isabelle and Nicolas saw a group of men working.
Among them, there were a few thin, small boys also swinging hoes.
One of the boys was so frail that he seemed to have no strength left to lift his hoe.
The sailboat sped along, barely skimming the ground.
Isabelle, Nicolas, and Elouise pulled the exhausted boy into the boat. This new friend was named Rashid.
Elouise used Rashid's tattered scarf to wipe the sweat from his forehead.
Sidonie placed her own feathers as a cushion for Rashid.

[P10] "What is that dark, smoky cloud?" Isabelle called out.

[P11] "Look, we're above a huge city, and everything here is smoking! Houses, factories, cars, people..."

Before Eluise could finish speaking, she started coughing.
Rashid and Nicola also covered their noses and coughed nonstop.
Even Sidonie was no exception.
Isabelle shouted angrily, "Don't those people see that boy? He's almost suffocating from the smoke!"

[P12] "This time it's my turn to act!"
Gus said, diving into the thick smoke.

[P13] Rashid said to the boy, 'Take a deep breath, Eric! Is the air here
especially fresh?'
Six passengers floated freely in the air with the sailboat.
Suddenly, a series of dull booms echoed through the sky.
'I've never been afraid of storms!' Isabel shouted loudly.

[P14] This huge noise was not lightning, nor thunder, but the explosion of shells and the gunfire of machine guns.
The children in the sailboat were frightened and huddled together tightly.
Sidonie poked her head out and looked: "A woman is running with a child in her arms..."

"We must get away from here quickly!" Isabelle cried out, "Wait, we should go save them!"

[P15] "It must be the child in the woman's arms who saw our sailboat," said Sidonie.

Everyone reached out their hands, Sidonie used its claws, and they helped the woman named Magda and her child, Lila, onto the boat.

The sailboat soared back into the sky, carefully
avoiding the bullets flying everywhere.

[P16] But the ship's hull was pierced, and the sail had several holes. The sailboat wobbled and lost its direction.

[P17] We've finally arrived at the beach again.
"We can dock here," said Nicolas.
"Be careful, there's a witch over there!" shouted Isabelle.

[P18] "No, she's my grandma!" Eluis was the first to get off the boat. "Grandma sells fish here, everyone knows her!"

[P19] Everyone worked together to flip the boat over so that Magda and Lila could rest.
Isabel and Erik took down the sail and made it into a hammock.
Rashid brought wood for a fire for everyone.
Nicolas took off one of the boat's wheels to use as a clothesline.
Sidney and Gus turned the other wheel into their bird's nest.
Eluis and his grandmother cooked a meal for everyone together.

[P20] Grandma's fish soup was delicious. She even added a 'flying fish' to the soup to help Sidney's shoulder heal faster.
"I really hope you can stay here a little longer," Grandma said.
"But, we each have our own families..." Nicola replied.
"And friends..." Rashid added.
"And we still have many important journeys to make..." Gus said.
Just then, Rashid pointed to an abandoned wooden house on the beach: "With those planks, we might be able to build a flying sailboat three times bigger than this one!"

[P21] The grandmother excitedly stood up: "Rashid is right! I'll go find my old sheets, old skirts, and old handkerchiefs, and I'll sew you the biggest and most beautiful sail in the world!"
At that moment, Sidoine slowly flew into the air: "Wow, I can fly again! Who wants to ride on my back?"

[P22] "Tomorrow at dawn, we'll set off!" said Nicola, "riding our sailboat, flying into the vast, boundless sky..."

[P23] The author's name is Quentin Blake from the UK, but he did not complete this picture book alone. Children from Singapore, the UK, Ireland, France, and Norway—1800 in total—helped him create it.
Over the course of a year, these children communicated with Quentin Blake through letters, drawings, and emails, discussing various issues facing their shared home—Earth: war, pollution, child labor, and conflict... After listening to children's hopes and dreams for a warmer, better world, Quentin Blake created 'The Sailboat in the Sky'.
We thank Genevieve Ruga and the Reading Enlightenment Association (LSA-17), the founders and coordinators of this project, and all the children who participated. Their names are printed on the endpapers of this book.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《天上的帆船》的封面，展示了孩子们乘坐一辆带有红色风帆的木车在蓝天白云间飞翔的场景，周围有几只白鹳相伴，画面充满童趣与想象力。
[P3] 本页为绘本《天上的帆船》的扉页，展示了书名、作者、译者及出版社信息，并配有五个孩子和一只小狗的插图，其中一个孩子指向天空，似乎在讲述或想象着什么。
[P4] 伊莎贝尔和尼古拉在沙滩上散步，随意穿过沙丘，画面中可见沙滩、枯木和远处的海天。
[P5] 伊莎贝尔和尼古拉在沙滩上发现了一艘破旧的帆船，他们决定一起把它拉出来，并在修理过程中发现这艘船看起来有些古怪。
[P6] 沙丘上吹起海风，帆船在沙滩上滑行，伊莎贝尔注意到一只受伤的鹳，它自称西多尼，因肩膀受伤无法飞翔。
[P7] 帆船在海风中飞向天空，孩子们救下的受伤鹳西多尼也一同飞起。一只名叫古斯的鹅飞来，建议他们帮助更多无法飞翔的同伴，并主动提出带路。
[P8] 帆船飞到另一片沙滩上空，发现一群男孩正在追打一个女孩，西多尼警告他们可能会伤到女孩的肩膀。伊莎贝尔伸出援手，将女孩救上船，女孩名叫艾卢伊斯。
[P9] 帆船飞过一片工地，伊莎贝尔、尼古拉和艾卢伊斯发现一个瘦弱的男孩在辛苦劳作，便将他救上船，并用围巾为他擦汗，西多尼还用羽毛为他垫靠垫。
[P10] 帆船在空中飞行，伊莎贝尔注意到前方一片黑乎乎的烟雾，感到疑惑并出声询问。
[P11] 帆船飞过一座被浓烟笼罩的城市，孩子们和鹳西多尼因烟雾而咳嗽，伊莎贝尔愤怒地指出烟雾正威胁着一个男孩的呼吸。
[P12] 古斯主动飞入浓烟中，准备采取行动，而帆船上的孩子们和鹳西多尼则在烟雾中飞行，画面中还可见一个孩子在轮椅上被推着，似乎正被烟雾所困。
[P13] 帆船在空中自由飘荡，拉希德提醒男孩呼吸新鲜空气，伊莎贝尔则在巨响中大声表示自己从不害怕暴风雨。
[P14] 帆船飞过一片战火纷飞的废墟，炮弹爆炸和枪声四起，孩子们惊恐蜷缩。鹳西多尼发现一位抱着孩子的妇女在逃命，伊莎贝尔在惊慌中仍坚持要前去救援。
[P15] 在战火纷飞的废墟中，孩子们和鹳西多尼救下了一位抱着孩子的妇女玛格达和她的孩子里拉，并将他们安置到帆船上，随后帆船飞向天空，躲避四处飞来的子弹。
[P16] 帆船在飞行中遭到破坏，船身被打穿，船帆破损，导致它在空中摇晃并失去方向。
[P17] 帆船飞抵海滩，尼古拉提议靠岸，伊莎贝尔则警告大家前方有个巫婆。
[P18] 帆船抵达海滩，艾卢伊斯第一个下船，指着一位绿皮肤的老妇人说那是他的外婆，并解释她在这里卖鱼，大家都认识她。
[P19] 在海滩上，孩子们和鹳西多尼、古斯一起动手，将破损的帆船改造成临时住所，用船帆做吊床、轮子做晾衣架和鸟巢，并由艾卢伊斯和外婆一起为大家做饭，营造出温馨的避难所。
[P20] 在海滩上，外婆为孩子们做了美味的鱼汤，大家围坐一起用餐。尽管孩子们因家人和旅程而不得不离开，拉希德却提议用废弃木屋的木板建造一艘更大的会飞帆船。
[P21] 外婆决定用旧布料为孩子们缝制一艘新船帆，西多尼则兴奋地飞向空中，邀请孩子们骑上它的背。
[P22] 尼古拉宣布明天黎明将乘坐帆船出发，飞向广阔的天空，画面中鹳西多尼在空中飞翔，帆船在粉色云朵间飞行。
[P23] 本页为绘本《天上的帆船》的版权页和致谢页，介绍了作者昆廷·布莱克与全球1800名儿童共同创作本书的过程，并列出了出版信息、版权数据及致谢内容。
